summary: Cowlitz County pole-tower lookout built 1942 and lost in 1963; the summit is wooded and remnants are hard to find, and a tree-farm permit is needed.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with 7x7 foot cab and a ground house at its base
facts.status_note: The tower and house came down in 1963; the summit is wooded and remnants are hard to find

access.note: Roads reach the site on Weyerhaeuser tree farm land; Will Hite's guide says a St. Helens Tree Farm Permit is needed to be legal

visit.trail_note: Roads go to within feet of the site; a short spur road blocked with a trench leads to the open site

events.note: 40-foot pole tower with 7x7 cab and ground house

corrections.why: FFLOS and Firelookout.com give 5,153 ft (1,571 m); Will Hite's guide gives 2,149 to 2,160 feet and calls it a low-elevation mountain. The 5,153 figure looks like the outlier, but check a USGS map before changing it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1963; Firelookout.com and Will Hite's guide say destroyed in 1963. Will Hite ties the loss to the Columbus Day storm, which Wikipedia names as 1962, so the year is unsettled.

sources.title: Meridian Mountain Lookout - Weyerhaeuser Tree Farm

notes_for_editor: Record coordinates match FFLOS (46.2099, -122.73706). Elevation conflicts: FFLOS and Firelookout give 5,153 ft; Will Hite gives 2,149 to 2,160 ft. See corrections. The 1963 loss date appears in all three lookout sources, but Will Hite ties it to the Columbus Day storm, which Wikipedia dates to 1962. Staffing rests on one name (Dennis Gross, 1953) from Firelookout.com only. Access is 'permission' per the guide's tree-farm permit note; the permit rules were not checked against the landowner.
